problem: Vision-only navigation policies ignore embodiment geometry, so the same observation can imply different actions for different agents. Prior embodiment-aware work relies on RL or simulated data, or (ExAug) constrains discrete waypoints, which misses collision risk in continuous space.
motivation: Embodiments differ in size and traversability (a cat fits through a gap a car must detour around), so vision alone cannot yield reliable trajectories for a specific body. RL is costly and unstable, so an imitation-learning route that supports large-scale pretraining and real-world fine-tuning is needed. Real navigation data has very few high-risk samples, so risk perception and correction need synthetic augmentation.
key_idea: Inject embodiment geometry (L, W, H, max traversable height) as a conditional token in pretraining on multi-embodiment Internet video, then in fine-tuning add decoupled Spatial Perception and Risk-Aware Correction modules trained on augmented high-risk trajectories.
insight: Explicit embodiment conditioning helps consistently but modestly in pretraining, because image sequences already implicitly encode some embodiment cues. Risk augmentation is what makes perception work: TPR rises from about 9-29% to about 71-85% with almost no added false alarms. In the appendix ablation, letting sub-module losses update the context (Sub-Grad) and using a unidirectional mask lower the perception and correction losses (0.020→0.012 and 0.195→0.162 with Sub-Grad).
method: Input Encoder: DINOv3-S RGB and ConvNeXt-T depth tokens, plus goal and embodiment-geometry tokens (m∈R^4), form 130 context tokens; a unidirectional cross-attention mask lets action queries read the context without altering it.
Action Prediction: decodes 8 action queries into an 8-step action sequence with behavior cloning, then converts it to a local waypoint trajectory and trajectory features.

Spatial Perception: a transformer over the context and trajectory features regresses the nearest-obstacle distance per waypoint; it is sequential rather than parallel to action prediction, so augmented high-risk trajectories can be substituted in, and its loss updates the shared context.

Risk-Aware Correction: triggered only when predicted distance is below 0.5 m; it predicts multi-hot feasibility over 19 global yaw-offset bins (±45°, 5° step) and picks the feasible bin with the smallest |angle|.

Risk Trajectory Augmentation: fuse future depth frames into a local point cloud, fit the ground with RANSAC, and inflate obstacles by embodiment size into an occupancy grid. Scale and rotate spline-smoothed trajectories, label colliding ones as risky, and use collision-free ones as feasible correction bins.

Cross-embodiment dataset: about 1000 h of YouTube first-person video across 8 embodiment categories, pseudo-labeled with Depth-Anything-3 (scale-consistent rather than metric) with manual geometry annotation and smoothness filtering; a mini HM3D is added.
Two-stage training: pretraining optimizes only the action branch with BC; fine-tuning on GND, SCAND-Spot and SiT jointly optimizes action, perception and correction with a weighted sum.

setting.backbone: DINOv3-S (frozen) + ConvNeXt-T depth encoder + 6-layer transformer (384-d) with decoupled heads, trained by IL
setting.training_data: Pretraining on ~1000 h of Internet first-person video (8 embodiments, Depth-Anything-3 pseudo-labels) plus mini HM3D; fine-tuning on GND, SCAND-Spot and SiT with risk trajectory augmentation
setting.observation: RGB image history (k=4) + current depth, relative 2D goal, embodiment geometry vector
setting.action_space: 8-step sequence of linear/angular velocities [v,w] converted to local waypoints; global yaw correction in 5° bins
setting.privileged: none at test time (occupancy grids from future depth used only for offline augmentation)

results: With correction, EA-Nav beats NavDP on the two harder simulation scenes (SR 0.62 vs 0.60 on Scene2, 0.60 vs 0.56 on Scene3), but trails it on Scene1 (0.70 vs 0.73 SR). In the real world it is best or near-best across Go2 and TurtleBot, with much lower collision rates than iPlanner, NavDP, NoMaD and ExAug for the larger bodies, e.g. Go2 Body++ SR 0.60 with CR 0.00 against 0.00 SR for all baselines. Augmentation lifts high-risk recognition about 5×.
limitations: Models only size geometry, not turning radius or motion constraints, so it cannot handle embodiments with different kinematics.
The real-data-only training set is smaller and less diverse than NavDP's synthetic data, leaving a sim gap; correction is weak at far range for small bodies.
Real-world evaluation is small (5 trials per setting) and on custom scenes.
